why_trail.why: The gate's one unmapped seam -- decision vs authorization -- resolves in fix A's favour. Everything downstream of the two clauses in verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py already handles stop: the installed G2 verifier lists stop in DECISIONS and sanctions current_wave:null only for it, and the renderer never reads current_wave at all. So the refusal is local to this script, not inherited from the seam it delegates to. The ordering wrinkle is real but shallow: boundary_id is needed to LOCATE the decision, so structure validation must stay ahead of policy -- split _next_wave into an unconditional structural half and a decision-aware authorization half called after REPLAN_RESULT is read. One nuance the ruling settles: 'may express no launch authorized' is permissive, so under stop launch_id is accepted either null or a valid SAFE_ID; that permissiveness is what lets the sanctioned assertion inversion at tests:466 (which keeps launch_id='wave-2') go green without a second fixture change.

GREEN. The restructure landed as two functions rather than one relaxed condition, because the ordering wrinkle is structural: _next_wave now checks only what is decision-independent (key set, boundary_id path safety, trigger), and _require_launch_authorization carries the policy and runs after REPLAN_RESULT is read. boundary_id validation stayed exactly where it was and stayed unconditional, so the stop condition about losing it never triggered. The one nuance worth recording: under stop the null launch_id is PERMITTED, not required, and the else-branch falls through to the same SAFE_ID check, so path safety on a present launch_id survives the relaxation -- asserted directly with a '../escape' launch_id that must still refuse. Selector green: exit 0, 2 passed, 24 deselected; the whole doctrine file is 26 passed / 25 subtests, exit 0, which covers the inverted assertion.

Mutation test green: exit 0, 1 test, 7 subtests, selector collects 1. Two things it taught me that the plan did not anticipate. First, my intended G2-breaking mutation was a no-op: emptying revised_forecast on the LIVE stop packet keeps it G2-valid, because an empty forecast is legitimate when the epic ends. Caught only because the assert-the-mutation-applied discipline is paired with an assert-it-went-red -- the subtest failed loudly instead of passing vacuously. Swapped to blanking revised_epic_body, the field CURRENT_TRUTH.md is actually written from. Second, I proved the test has teeth rather than asserting it: temporarily over-relaxed the code to 'null launch_id skips authorization' (the plausible wrong shape), and repair_names_no_launch caught it -- a repair packet sailed through with exit 0. Restored and re-verified; both selectors green. Also worth recording for the reviewer: an early-return-on-stop shape is caught by m1's golden test, not this one, because that test asserts the two Markdown writes actually happened.

Coupled suite exit 0: 390 passed / 487 subtests against the 387 / 480 baseline at HEAD 6f48ece4. The delta is +3 tests and +7 subtests, and every unit of it is mine: the 3 tests are the two stop_boundary golden-path methods plus the one stop_mutation method, and the 7 subtests are that method's 7 mutation subTests. Nothing else moved -- in particular the sanctioned inversion changed an assertion INSIDE an existing subTest (launch_authority='stop'), so it shifts no count, which is the cleanest evidence that the inversion swapped an expectation rather than adding or removing coverage. No red anywhere, so nothing to float from the suite. The two CRLF-artifact files under transitions/close-to-w5/ were left unstaged and untouched as instructed.
